name: Rastaban
description: A star 117 parsecs away, 40 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: radius 40.284 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 996.471 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.05) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: effective temperature 5113 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.049)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.05 from 2024A&A...692A.189R; the 24 published values span log g 1.35 to 2.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 85670: RV -21 +/- 0.23 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: distance 116.55 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A star 117 parsecs away, 40 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 996 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,113 K, so 40.284 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 85670: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Draconis
quotes.card: Beta Draconis is a binary star system and the third-brightest star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Draco.
quotes.introduction: The two components are designated Beta Draconis A and B respectively.
